mentions.name: CLI Argument Specification and Parser
mentions.description: A CLI argument specification with an implementing parser, designed to standardize command-line argument conventions as an alternative to Python's argparse — supporting consistent usage/help invocation and predictable behavior when no arguments are given.
mentions.problem: Frustrated with Python's argparse and with inconsistent argument conventions across work tools, where pulling up a usage string might require help, -h, --help, -help, +help, or +<prog>.help, and not all scripts display a usage string when no args are given.
mentions.audience: Developers writing command-line programs and scripts
mentions.source_excerpt: A CLI argument specification and a parser that implements it. Mostly because I’m annoyed with Python’s argparse, so I’m adding blackjack and removing hookers.

evidence.value: A CLI argument specification and a parser that implements it. Mostly because I’m annoyed with Python’s argparse, so I’m adding blackjack and removing hookers.
